public_claim: A cross-source record supports same-site continuity between Chandler Jaycees BMX and today’s Chandler BMX: a BMX history timeline says Merl Mennenga started Chandler Jaycees in 1975 and that the track remained in the same location; a June 1987 BMX Plus! retrospective identifies Chandler Jaycees as the ABA’s first track; and current USA BMX places Chandler BMX at Frye and McQueen while describing it as the first BMX track the ABA opened for sanctioned racing.
evidence_character: CROSS-SOURCE SYNTHESIS — SPECIALIST SITE CONTINUITY + PERIOD TRACK IDENTITY + CURRENT FIRST-PARTY SITE
confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH FOR SAME PHYSICAL SITE; EXACT HISTORICAL COURSE GEOMETRY OPEN
evidence_boundary: This supports Chandler Jaycees BMX and current Chandler BMX occupying the same physical track site at the Frye/McQueen ground. It does not establish the exact 1975 or 1979–1983 dirt-course center, identical course geometry through time, every operator or sanction transition, uninterrupted organizational identity under one legal entity, or an exact 1975 street-address formulation. The historical map point therefore represents the shared site at SITE_POINT_APPROXIMATE precision, while the current Chandler point remains EXACT_TRACK_POINT.
growth_release: v0.48 chandler jaycees site continuity recovery 1
admission_basis: A specialist BMX history explicitly states Chandler Jaycees remained in the same location; the period BMX Plus! record independently identifies Chandler Jaycees as the ABA’s first track, while current USA BMX identifies the Frye/McQueen Chandler facility as the first track the ABA opened for sanctioned racing. Together these sources clear a same-physical-site threshold without clearing exact historical course geometry or every organizational transition.
